title.text: Philippine International Hot Air Balloon Fiesta

title_en.text: Philippine International Hot Air Balloon Fiesta

tagline.text: A February sky festival that began in Clark and now flies at New Clark City

location.label: Location
location.text: New Clark City, Capas, Tarlac (formerly the Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Every February (February 13–15 in 2026; check each year)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱750–1,800 (based on a 2026 general admission ticket of ₱750 plus the optional evening event at ₱1,800)

children.text: The Philippine International Hot Air Balloon Fiesta is an air sports festival that began in the Clark Freeport Zone in 1994. Around February each year it features colorful hot air balloons, night glow, and drone and paragliding events. Since 2024 it has been held at New Clark City in Capas, Tarlac.

The Philippine International Hot Air Balloon Fiesta (PIHABF) is one of the longest-running air sports events in the Philippines. According to Wikipedia, it was first held in 1994 at the Clark Parade Grounds in the Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga, and was started to help nearby communities recover from the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo. The founders are listed as then Tourism Secretary Mina Gabor, John Emery of British Airways, and South Korean balloonist Sung Kee Paik. The first edition had 21 pilots from 11 countries.

The festival has been held most years since, but there were gaps. In 1999 it was not held because of funding problems and concerns about flights at Clark International Airport, and it returned in 2000. It was not held in 2014, when the Department of Tourism held a similar event separately in April, and it was canceled in 2019 because organizers could not get firm commitments from government partners. In 2020 it was held at San Lazaro Leisure Park in Carmona, Cavite, and it was not held from 2021 to 2023 because of COVID-19. It returned in 2024 as the 24th edition.

The current venue is New Clark City in Capas, Tarlac. It has been held there since 2024, and the 26th edition in 2026 took place over Valentine's weekend, February 13–15. We placed this entry in the Tarlac and Zambales region to match the venue, but because it is close to Clark International Airport and connected to the Clark area in Pampanga, many people call it the Clark balloon festival. Check the official website (philballoonfest.net) and Facebook for the dates and venue of the next edition.

The 2026 event was described as combining 22 special-shape balloons, a 550-drone show, night glow, a paragliding accuracy competition, FPV drone racing, drone soccer and a hoverbike demonstration with car drifting, kite flying and a fly market. It is not just an event for watching balloons; it is a family event that lets you enjoy aviation as a whole.

Morning balloon launches are said to start as early as 6:30. The wind is calm at sunrise, which makes for the best scenes. One guide recommends arriving at the venue by 5:00 a.m. to see the sunrise launch.

In 2026, balloons such as Finley the Turtle from the UK and the Tuca the Toucan, Macaws and Walrus from Brazil made their Philippine debut, and regulars such as Yoda, Princess Nelly and the Busby returned. The balloons that appear change every year, so check the official introductions.

blocks.title: Night glow and the Valentine's dinner

children.text: Night glow, when the balloons are lit up in the evening, is a symbol of this festival. In 2026 a Valentine's dinner (February 14) was held for a separate fee of
, with balloons and drones lighting the scene.

A 550-drone show, FPV drone racing, drone soccer, a paragliding accuracy competition and a paramotor beach ball competition were announced. Pilots from several countries are said to take part in the competitions.

There are RC airplanes, a paper airplane contest, kite flying, an ultralight aircraft display by the Angeles Flying Club, helicopter demonstration flights, car drifting and a fly market (food and souvenirs). There are many programs to enjoy with children.

There is an aviation seminar covering flight operations, safety and new technology, which students, aviation enthusiasts and industry professionals can attend. The ticket that includes the seminar was listed at ₱1,000.

blocks.title: The open grounds of New Clark City

children.text: New Clark City is a new-town development district with facilities such as an athletics stadium, and it has been the venue of this festival since 2024. The specific launch areas and layout within the venue may differ each year, and the coordinates for this entry are near the athletics stadium.

blocks.title: Pilots and visitors from around the world

children.text: Wikipedia says that more than 100 balloon pilots now gather from around the world and about 100,000 people visit each year. In 2024 a skydiving Philippine flag jump was held for the first time. Visitor numbers vary each year, so treat them as a rough reference only.

items.title: From Manila by car or taxi

children.text: From Manila, take NLEX toward Clark and Capas. In 2026, guide billboards were reportedly put up along NLEX.
The access roads can be blocked on event days, so it is better to travel in the early hours. Parking arrangements differ each year, so check the official announcements.
If you drive, you can reduce the parking burden by carpooling and leaving early. One guide also recommends carpooling and leaving early.
In 2026 there was free transport arranged with local governments, which was described as linking the transport systems of Capas, Bamban and Clark.
The usual way is to take a bus from Manila toward Clark, go as close as you can, and then use a shuttle. Check operators and fares locally.
Whether there is an official shuttle and where it boards change every year.
New Clark City is fairly close to Clark International Airport (CRK). Check the exact travel time and fare locally.
If you arrive at Manila's airport (MNL), the overland trip takes time, so allow plenty of time in your schedule.

The balloon festival is held in February. Wikipedia says it takes place between January and February, and in 2026 it was February 13–15. February is dry season in the Philippines, with little rain and many clear days, which makes it the best time for ballooning.

During the day, early morning and sunset, when the wind is weak, are suitable for launches. The midday sun is strong and hot, so bring a hat and sunscreen, and since it may be chilly around sunrise, a light jacket is handy.

The venue is New Clark City, so many people stay in the nearby Clark and Angeles area. Hann Resorts and Casino has been named as an official hotel partner. Rooms fill up quickly on festival weekends, so book early.

Inside the venue, the fly market serves as a bazaar selling food, local products and souvenirs. Lines can be long at midday, so it is easier to go early or in the early afternoon. Bring plenty of water and a hat.

When the festival runs three days, as in 2026, you can choose one of the second and third days. Visitors usually crowd in on weekends (Saturday and Sunday), so going on a Friday is worth considering if you want to enjoy it at leisure. Programs differ from day to day, so check the timetable for the events you want to see first.
Tickets are also sold on site, but you can reportedly buy them in advance through HelixPay, SM Tickets and Klook. One guide also says sunrise entry slots sell out quickly.
To see the early-morning launch, arrive by 5:00 a.m. Leave early in the morning.
Bring sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses, and since mornings can be chilly, a light jacket is helpful.
Bring a power bank for your phone. You will be taking a lot of photos and video.
Balloon launches are delayed or canceled depending on wind and weather. Planning two days is safer than going for just one.
At the launch area, follow the instructions of safety staff and do not go near the balloons without permission.
Check the latest schedule at philballoonfest.net and the official Facebook page.

Tickets come in types such as general, with seminar and VIP. If your main aim is to watch balloons, check the official announcements to see whether a general ticket is enough and what each type includes.
Balloon events are very sensitive to wind and weather. Launches may be delayed or canceled, so check the change and refund conditions before buying tickets.
The venue and dates change from year to year. In the past it was held at the Clark Parade Grounds, Carmona and New Clark City, among other places, and some years it was skipped.
Roads can be congested on event days and parking may be limited, so plan to arrive early and use the shuttle.
The midday heat is strong. Pay attention to hydration and rest.
Watch for theft of belongings and carry cash in small amounts split across pockets.
Do not fly a personal drone while drones and balloons are in the sky.
